name: Infinera San Jose fab

parties.name: Nokia
parties.note: Infinera became a wholly owned Nokia subsidiary when the merger closed on 2025-02-28.

parties.name: U.S. Department of Commerce
parties.note: Direct funding agreement signed on 16 January 2025 covering this fab and a Pennsylvania packaging and test site, after preliminary terms in October 2024.

summary: Infinera, a Nokia subsidiary since February 2025, plans a new fab in San Jose, California for indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits. The CHIPS program finalized up to USD 93 million in January 2025, shared with a new packaging and test facility in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, and expects the two projects to raise Infinera's U.S. capacity about tenfold. Funding is paid against milestones such as facility development and production qualification, and the award page targeted production in summer 2026.

metrics.note: Split between the San Jose fab and the Bethlehem, Pennsylvania packaging and test facility; paid as capital spending, facility development, production qualification and other milestones are met.
Expected capital expenditure the undated final-award page gives for both Infinera projects together.
Manufacturing jobs for the California project on the undated final-award page, which also lists 700 construction jobs for it.

milestones.note: Preliminary CHIPS terms announced on 17 October 2024.
The CHIPS project page expects production in summer 2026.

notes: The CHIPS page gives two different construction-job figures for the California project (700 and 1,000) and describes the work both as a new fab and as construction and modernization of a fab and foundry facility. Searches in November 2026 found no report of construction progress or production at the new fab, and Nokia's plans for it after the acquisition were not found.

registry_records.note: Infinera's award also covers a test and packaging plant in Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, which has its own registry row.

review.method: Independent AI-assisted review (Claude): re-opened every cited source, checked each statement against it and searched for newer reporting.
review.changes: Changed the parent company to Nokia, which has owned Infinera since February 2025; set the undated CHIPS project page's publication date to null and redated its figures to the final award; added the milestone-based payment terms from the 10-K.
